# *stareal* <img src="man/figures/logo.png" align="right" height="139" alt="" />

**Spatial-temporal areal estimation from survey data.**

**Status: in development. Current release: 0.2.0.**

> ### 📖 Documentation: [mrc-ide.github.io/stareal](https://mrc-ide.github.io/stareal/)
>
> Tutorials, the method, and the reference for every function are there.
> This GitHub page holds the source code only.

*stareal* fits a Bayesian space-time model to binomial survey data, such as
the prevalence of a drug-resistance marker, at an areal level:
administrative units, or any other set of polygons. Time runs in regular
steps of your choosing, such as months, quarters or years. The model
estimates prevalence in every area and time step, including the many with
no surveys, and gives the uncertainty of every estimate. Regional and
national summaries are made from the joint posterior.

It is built for data that are sparse relative to the space-time grid.
Standard areal software carries a latent value for every area-time cell,
surveyed or not. *stareal* integrates the unsurveyed cells out exactly,
fits the model to the surveyed cells alone, and rebuilds the full surface
from each posterior draw. Its cost depends on the number of surveys, not
on the size of the map.

The model offers five spatial priors (Leroux, BYM2, the proper and the
intrinsic CAR, and independent areas), optional main effects in space and
in time (including random walks), and Knorr-Held's four types of
space-time interaction. Models are compared by approximate leave-one-out
from a single fit each, or by cross-validation.

## Installation

```r
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("mrc-ide/stareal@v0.2.0")
```

This installs release 0.2.0, which never changes. For results that do not
move as the package develops, install a release like this and report its
version. `remotes::install_github("mrc-ide/stareal")` gives the latest
release.

## A first map

```r
library(stareal)
iso3 <- c("DJI", "ERI", "ETH", "KEN", "SOM", "SSD", "SDN", "UGA")      # the eight IGAD countries
adm1 <- sf::st_as_sf(geodata::gadm(iso3, level = 1, path = tempdir(), resolution = 2))
adm1 <- adm1[adm1$ENGTYPE_1 != "Water body", ]                          # lakes are not places
fr <- areal_frame(adm1, id = "GID_1", groups = c(country = "COUNTRY"),
                  link_within = "country")                               # areas and their neighbours
tf <- time_frame(1989, 2024, "month")                                    # the time grid
d  <- areal_data(igad_crt76t, fr, tf, y = "positive", k = "tested",
                 coords = c("longitude", "latitude"), date = "collection_day")
fit <- fit_areal(d)                                                      # MCMC, chains in parallel
diagnose(fit)                                                            # convergence of every parameter
pr <- predict(fit, groups = "country")                                   # every area-month, and countries
plot(pr, time = "2024-01")
```

The data are the chloroquine-resistance marker crt K76T in the eight IGAD
countries, from the public [STAVE](https://github.com/mrc-ide/STAVE)
collation. The boundaries are GADM's, downloaded through
[geodata](https://cran.r-project.org/package=geodata). The
[package website](https://mrc-ide.github.io/stareal/) has tutorials, from
this analysis to rare markers, covariates, cross-validation and simulation
studies.
